description: Reported Trishuli River stage changes at Galchhi and Malekhu during the 26 August 2026 Lhende Khola / Bhote Koshi / Trishuli flood, transcribed from an ICIMOD media advisory. These are quoted figures from public reporting, not gauge records; no time series was retrievable (Nepal DHM gauges have no open API, RELEASE_STATUS.md Known gaps 2). Every value carries the sentence it was read from.

sources.publisher: ICIMOD (International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development)
sources.title: Major flash flood sweeps through Nepal's Rasuwa district, raising fears of further downstream flooding
sources.licence: ICIMOD (c) 2026. All rights reserved; cited-only (page not stored)
sources.notes: sha256 and size are of the HTML bytes retrieved with curl on 2026-09-03; the page is all-rights-reserved so only short quotations are kept here. The page attributes the Malekhu figure to DHM in an image caption ('Rapid rise in Trisuli River water level at Malekhu. Source: DHM.').

stations.name: Trishuli River at Galchhi (spelled 'Galchchi' and 'Glachchi' in the source)
Trishuli River at Malekhu
stations.operator: DHM (per the source's image caption 'Source: DHM')

observations.time_basis: not_stated_in_source: the advisory gives no clock time for this rise; it reports that Bhote Koshi basin levels 'began rising rapidly around 9:00 AM local time on August 26' (NPT, UTC+05:45)
observations.excerpt: Water levels on the Trishuli River at Galchchi reportedly rose by as much as nine metres within 30 minutes, while levels at Malekhu increased by seven metres over a similar period.
observations.notes: 'as much as' - the figure is an upper reported value; 'reportedly' - ICIMOD relays it rather than measuring it.

observations.time_basis: not_stated_in_source: 'over a similar period' to the Galchhi rise; no clock time given
observations.excerpt: Water levels on the Trishuli River at Galchchi reportedly rose by as much as nine metres within 30 minutes, while levels at Malekhu increased by seven metres over a similar period.
observations.notes: interval_s = 1800 is read from 'over a similar period' relative to the 30-minute Galchhi figure.

excerpts: According to local reports, water levels in the Bhote Koshi basin began rising rapidly around 9:00 AM local time on August 26.
Several water monitoring stations along the Trishuli River were reportedly damaged or washed away during the event, although the Glachchi monitoring station remains operational.
